title: Entry-Level Remote Data Analyst at cewit New York, NY
description:
Entry-Level Remote Data Analyst job at cewit. New York, NY.


 Job Overview
 We are seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Entry-Level Data Analyst to join our remote team. This role is an excellent opportunity for individuals looking to build a career in data analysis with ample opportunities for growth and professional development. You will be responsible for collecting, analyzing, and interpreting data to provide insights that support business decisions. No prior experience is necessary as we will provide comprehensive training for the right candidate.




 Key Responsibilities
 
 Collect, clean, and organize data from various sources to ensure data accuracy and completeness.
 Perform data analysis using statistical methods and software tools to uncover trends, patterns, and insights.
 Create visual reports and dashboards to communicate findings clearly to stakeholders.
 Assist in the development of data models and predictive analytics to support decision-making processes.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams (such as marketing, sales, and operations) to understand data needs and provide relevant insights.
 Continuously monitor data quality and identify areas for improvement in data collection and analysis processes.
 Maintain confidentiality of sensitive company data and adhere to data protection regulations.
 


 Qualifications
 
 Bachelor's degree: in a related field (e.g. Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, or a similar discipline) is preferred but not required.
 Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
 Basic knowledge of statistical analysis and data visualization tools (such as Excel, Power BI, or Tableau) is a plus.
 Familiarity with SQL or other database languages is preferred but not mandatory.
 Strong problem-solving skills and ability to think critically.
 Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.
 Self-motivated and able to work independently in a remote setting.
 Ability to manage time effectively and meet deadlines.
 


 Experience
 
 No prior work experience is required for this entry-level role.
 Familiarity with data analysis concepts through coursework, internships, or personal projects is advantageous.
 


 Benefits
 
 Salary: Competitive starting rate of $45,000 - $85,000 per year (based on experience and qualifications).
 Work-from-home flexibility: Enjoy the convenience of working remotely with flexible hours.
 Health Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance plans.
 Retirement Plan: 401(k) with company matching to help you plan for your future.
 Paid Time Off: Generous vacation days, paid sick leave, and holidays.
 Professional Development: Access to training programs and courses to enhance your data analysis skills and career progression.
 Career Growth Opportunities: Clear pathways for promotion and development into more advanced roles in data science and analytics.
 


 How to Apply
 We encourage you to apply if you are passionate about data, eager to learn and excited about starting a career in data analysis.

title: Associate Data Analyst, Clinical Data
description:
NYU Langone Health is hiring a Associate Data Analyst, Clinical Data with 0 - 3 years of experience. Based in United States -  New York, NY and with In-office ways of working. 
  
  Job description and responsibilities: 

NYU Langone Hospital - Brooklyn is a full-service teaching hospital and Level I trauma center located in Sunset Park, Brooklyn. The hospital is central to a comprehensive network of affiliated ambulatory and outpatient practices, and serves as NYU Langone Health's anchor for healthcare access, growth, and delivery in the entire borough. At NYU Langone Health, equity, diversity, and inclusion are fundamental values. We strive to be a place where our exceptionally talented faculty, staff, and students of all identities can thrive. We embrace diversity, inclusion, and individual skills, ideas, and knowledge. Learn more about NYU Langone Hospital – Brooklyn, and interact with us on LinkedIn, Glassdoor, Indeed, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube and Instagram.


Position Summary


We have an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Associate Clinical Data Analyst - Brooklyn.


In this role, the successful candidate The infection prevention and control (IPC) clinical data analyst will oversee and assist with the transformation of data into information to guide clinicians, support staff, and administration as we work to eliminate all preventable hospital-acquired infections (HAI) at NYULH. This analyst will be responsible for:



Ensuring HAI data are entered into local, state and federal government databases to ensure external reporting compliance
Helping to support health system efforts to maximize patient safety and efficiency
Supporting process improvements and standardizationacross the IPC data team
Assisting specifically with data systems and processes at the NYULH-Brooklyn campus, spending time in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, as required

The analyst will contribute to the development, implementation and success of hospital-wide IPC projects and initiatives.


Job Responsibilities



Ensure that data on HAIs and antimicrobial stewardship are reported routinely to the National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) and to the centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) and complete appropriate validation procedures
Ensure that reportable conditions are sent to the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
Respond to data requests and prepare internal reports on HAIs as needed
Participate in infection control projects in a hospital setting, such as environmental surveillance sampling
Help to stabilize and improve existing data processes and work with others in IPC to standardize protocols across the NYULH system
Work collaboratively with others in order to support reporting needs
Focus specifically on data processes and needs at the NYULH-Brooklyn campus
Perform other duties as aligned with the mission and the values of the organization

 
  
  Requirements and qualifications: Minimum Qualifications



To qualify you must have a Bachelors degree in relevant field such as biostatistics, epidemiology, clinical informatics, information
management or public health, or similar field
Detail oriented and organized
Written and oral communication skills applicable to a wide variety of audiences.
Experience with collecting and analyzing health data with the ability to articulate findings.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Experience in at least 1 querying language (e.g., SAS, Stata, R, SPSS)
Preferred candidates will also have: Strong problem solving and critical thinking skills,
Ability to approach new problems and develop a systematic, comprehensive solution. Teams well with others but also able to work independently as needed. Ability to manage change and ambiguity in a fast-paced environment

Qualified candidates must be able to effectively communicate with all levels of the organization.
